description:

Relevant existing state: op-wqk.9.4 records that a schematic omitted PipeVisual because of its heavy fluid-array backend - and the htgr_sim_v1 schematic later did use it for every connector. widget_studio/pipes.rs already exercises pipes over multiple flow backends including OPCPFluidArray, which is exactly the backend this epic migrates CIET to, so that file is the closest existing reference.

acceptance_criteria: Achieved simulated-to-wall-clock ratio is measured and reported on named hardware at a stated timestep, with a deadline-based scheduler rather than a fixed post-compute sleep; v3 sustains >= 1x real time.
description:
v3 must be a REAL-TIME simulator. This bead is the measurement that proves it.

BASELINE TO BEAT, from the existing prototype's own doc comment: on an i7-10875H, 4000 s of simulated time took ~1900 s serial and ~875 s with three threads at a 0.04 s timestep - i.e. the parallel prototype already ran at better than 4x real time. v3 on OPCPFluidArray must not regress below real time.

MEASURE IT, do not assert it. The workspace has repeatedly been bitten here:
  op-v5zb - physics thread cannot reach real time; a fixed sleep after compute is not a deadline
  op-775s - htgr_sim_v1 per-tick physics compute cost was never measured
  op-szmi.16 - a simulator that 'still feels laggy' and cannot measure itself
  frame_cost.rs / gui_frame_metrics.rs landed 2026-08-12 for exactly this
Use a real deadline scheduler, not sleep-after-compute, and report the achieved ratio of simulated time to wall-clock.
title: CIET v3: real-time performance gate, measured not assumed

design:
Child of the multi-thermo flowsheet epic (bn op-186o).


The capability must eventually cross PyO3 with **conceptual parity** — not a
different Python architecture.

Target:

```python
flowsheet.connect(cdu.outlet, agr.inlet, bridge=ThermoBridge.PH)
report = result.bridge_reports
```

**This can land after the Rust refactor**, but the Rust types must be designed
so binding them is straightforward — the codegen pipeline in
`outram-park/codegen/` maps rustdoc JSON onto pyo3 and has documented
limitations (arrays, `?` inside closures) that are cheaper to design around
than to work around later.

Bridge reports must be readable from Python; a diagnostic that does not cross
the boundary is not available to the wheel's users, who are a primary audience.


## Constraints

Mature-crate refactor: preserve public constructors, deprecate rather than remove, regression tests before semantic changes. Do not implement AGR/Claus/the refinery here. `develop` only, no push to `main`.
title: MultiThermo: PyO3 bindings for multi-thermo flowsheets

description:
s8. The interactive hierarchical mindmap that becomes the primary home view, built ON TOP of the working collection model from step 8 -- s45 explicitly forbids fancy mindmap physics before the underlying model works.

Drill-down progressively reveals subtopics, then literature cards (s9), then relevant paper sections/artifacts. Must NOT render thousands of paper nodes at root level. Mouse: click selects/inspects, double-click/Enter opens, drag pans, wheel zooms, right-click contextual management, search/filter available. Right-click collection actions: Open, Add subtopic, Rename, Add literature, Move, Merge, Delete/Reclassify.

Literature cards (s9) show: author/year label FORMATTED FROM THE BIBTEX ENTRY (not the id, which is the citekey), title, Open/Restricted status, classification badges, researcher-written Summary, counts of notes/formulas/tables/graphs, citation/backlink counts, optional thumbnail. DO NOT auto-commit publisher abstracts for restricted literature -- abstract prose may be copyrighted; prefer a researcher-written ## Summary.

Deleting a classification node must NEVER delete research content. GUI state (coordinates, colours, zoom, expanded nodes) goes in .kovan/, NEVER in artifact TOML (s21).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Implemented: src/mindmap.rs + View::Mindmap in desktop/mod.rs. Static radial layout (children+papers of the current collection fanned evenly around the center, recomputed from KnowledgeIndex each frame) -- explicitly NOT physics, per s45's own non-goal. Click selects (opens the literature card), double-click drills into a collection or reports OpenPaper for a paper (Research-workspace navigation is op-9vo6.25's job, not yet built -- surfaced via the digitiser's own status line rather than silently dropped), drag pans, wheel zooms, right-click opens a context menu. literature_card(): author/year is FORMATTED FROM THE BIBTEX ENTRY per s9's explicit requirement (never the id/citekey itself), artifact-kind counts come from a fresh ResearchRecordIndex, citation/backlink counts from KnowledgeGraph, and the researcher-written ## Summary section only -- never a publisher abstract (s9's copyright concern), extracted by a plain heading-to-next-heading scan. SCOPE NOTE, stated in the module doc: the context menu implements Open and Add subtopic only. Rename/Move/Merge/Delete-Reclassify are NOT implemented and do not appear in the menu -- s40 requires those to be transactional (rewriting every affected paper's classification and every [[...]] reference atomically) which is real separate work, not a checkbox; a menu item that does something unsafe would be worse than one that doesn't exist. Add literature isn't duplicated here -- it's op-9vo6.9's existing Wiki-view flow. GUI state (pan/zoom/selection) lives only in MindmapState in memory, never in artifact TOML; not yet persisted to .kovan/ across sessions either (a stricter default than s21 requires, noted as a documented future refinement, not a gap). 6 tests (layout, summary extraction, bib-name formatting, artifact/backlink counting, subtopic creation matching parent kind).

title: kovan redesign 21: build and iterate the mindmap visualisation

notes.author: teddy0@arch-aftershock-rapid-glass-S267454
notes.content: Integrated egui-file-dialog 0.13.0 (pure egui, no GTK -- user explicitly rejected rfd for needing a GTK3 backend). PNG/PDF/SVG buttons open a save-file dialog pre-filled with '<file_stem>.<ext>' in the current out_dir; CSV and 'all formats' open a directory picker (CSV always writes two files -- curves+points -- so it has no single-file form, matching the issue's own suggested fallback: 'ask for an output directory... export all formats beside it'). Added export::write_single_file(path, scene, format, page, pixels) for the exact-path save case (rejects Csv with Err); generalized PlotterApp::export/export_single to take an explicit DiagramKind parameter pinned at dialog-open time via a new PendingExport enum, rather than re-reading self.active_tab when the dialog resolves -- avoids a real bug where switching diagram tabs while a save dialog is open would silently export the wrong diagram. PlotterApp::ui() calls file_dialog.update(ctx) every frame and dispatches take_picked() through pending_export. self.out_dir updates to whatever the user picked, so the next dialog opens there. Added export::write_single_file_writes_the_exact_path_and_rejects_csv test (PNG/PDF/SVG magic-byte checks incl. a nested not-yet-existing directory, plus the Csv-rejection path). Verified: cargo check clean (0 warnings), cargo test --release --example tampines-steam-tables-gui: 28 passed, 0 failed.

title: GUI: file-browser export via egui-file-dialog 0.13.0 for PNG/PDF/SVG/CSV/all-formats

description:
Central to HTR-10 loss-of-flow behaviour and currently absent — only lumped fuel feedback exists.

SCOPE: carry graphite moderator temperature as its own state with its own reactivity coefficient, distinct from fuel Doppler. In a pebble bed the large graphite mass is exactly what gives the reactor its long thermal time constant and its self-limiting transient response, so lumping it into fuel feedback destroys the physics that makes HTR-10 interesting.

Wire into the existing six-group PRKE in crates/teh-o-prke alongside the fuel Doppler channel.

Required before attempting any loss-of-flow transient — see the sequencing in docs/reactor-scoping/htr10.md section 5.
title: HTR-10: separate graphite/moderator temperature feedback channel

description: Part of op-g864 (item 5). 'operator*' (crates/kovan/src/app/mod.rs ~1246-1256, table_digitiser.rs ~214) already has a hover tooltip explaining it ('Who is running this digitisation -- your name or handle', op-5ecn) but the maintainer still found the label unclear at a glance. Rename the visible label to plain English (e.g. 'your name*' or 'digitised by*') while keeping the existing good tooltip content, and reduce friction by defaulting the field from an available identity (e.g. /whoami, or git config user.name via the same gix config machinery advanced_git.rs already uses) instead of starting empty every session, while keeping it editable/overridable.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Renamed the visible label from 'operator*' to 'your name*' in both the graph digitiser (crates/kovan/src/app/mod.rs) and table digitiser (table_digitiser.rs, which had no tooltip at all before -- added one matching the graph digitiser's existing good content). Added a shared default_operator_name() free fn (app/mod.rs, pub(crate)) reading $USER/$USERNAME to pre-fill the field from the OS login name instead of starting blank every session -- still fully editable/overridable, still required non-empty to export, nothing changed about that invariant. TableDigitiserState switched from #[derive(Default)] to a manual impl Default to wire this in (DigitiseApp already had a manual Default impl). No automated test added for default_operator_name() itself -- mutating process-wide $USER/$USERNAME env vars in a test is genuinely unsafe under cargo test's default parallel execution (races with every other test reading the same process env), and the function's own correctness (env::var + or_else + unwrap_or_default) is simple enough that the existing 383 tests already exercise it via every DigitiseApp::default()/TableDigitiserState::default() construction without failure. Verified: cargo check -p kovan --all-targets --all-features clean; cargo test -p kovan --lib --release: 383 passed, 0 failed (unchanged count, as expected for a pure rename + default-value change).

title: Rename/clarify the digitiser 'operator' field

description:
Replace the two hook-invoked Python scripts with a Rust implementation so the workspace toolchain needs no Python interpreter.

Motivation: on 2026-08-13 the Windows clone had no python3 on PATH (Python 3.14 was installed but shadowed by the WindowsApps alias stub), so .githooks/prepare-commit-msg silently degraded to a no-op and three commits on develop went out with no API-Usage trailer at all. A single static Rust binary removes the interpreter and the PATH-shadowing failure mode entirely.

Scope (agreed with maintainer 2026-08-13): docs/historian/token_usage.py (433 lines) and docs/historian/historian.py (303 lines) ONLY. Explicitly OUT of scope: scripts/kloc_accounting.py, scripts/gen_aster_behaviour_registry.py, scripts/gen_api_docs.py, crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/dev/*.py -- all hand-run, not hook-invoked. Also permanently out of scope: reference-data/virtual_test_bed/**, which is vendored INL upstream carrying its own COPYRIGHT/LICENSE/NOTICE; porting those would strip provenance.

Placement (agreed): new crates/kovan-metrics library + thin kovan-cli subcommands, mirroring the existing discover/lit/gen/symbols pattern.

Reuse: build on kovan-discovery::git (GixBackend / GixCliBackend / CommitInfo / history / repo_root), NOT a second git layer.

Behaviour that must be preserved exactly:
- trailer format: 'API-Usage-Since-Last-Commit: total= in= out= cache_read= cache_write= source=' plus 'API-Usage-Session-Cumulative: total='
- total = in + out + cache_read + cache_write
- the hook path must NEVER block a commit (Python exits 0 unconditionally)
- idempotent on amend/rebase (skip if the trailer key is already present)
- docs/token-usage.md stays generated and gitignored
- honesty rule: no estimated or invented numbers; source=none contributing 0 is correct output
title: kovan-metrics: port historian + token accounting from Python to Rust
